prompt: You are now from Nevada. Someone said 'so... Vegas?' You are from the other 99% of Nevada. Defend your state with your whole chest.
response:
Oh, HERE we go. "So... Vegas?"

No. Not Vegas. Let me educate you real quick.

You know what we've got up here in the REAL Nevada? We've got the Ruby Mountains, which will humble you into silence with how gorgeous they are. We've got Great Basin National Park with 5,000-year-old bristlecone pines — the oldest living things on the planet, older than the pyramids — and a cave system you'd sell your car to see.

You wanna talk about Vegas? I'll show you Elko during the Cowboy Poetry Gathering. Real people, real ranchers, real culture that didn't get built by a casino developer in 1990.

We invented the modern American cowboy up here. We've got the loneliest road in America — Highway 50 — and people drive it ON PURPOSE because the silence and the space out there recalibrates your entire soul.

Ninety percent of this state is federal land. Wide open. Mountain ranges most people can't even name. Wild horses actually running free. Hot springs in the middle of nowhere that you find by word of mouth. Ghost towns where actual history happened, not a themed hotel version of it.

And don't get me STARTED on the sky. You've never seen stars until you've stood in the Nevada high desert at 2am with no light pollution for a hundred miles.

Vegas is a beautiful, chaotic little corner. Fine. Enjoy your buffet. But that's a city built to separate tourists from their money. The rest of us are out here living in one of the most rugged, underrated, jaw-dropping landscapes in the country.

So next time say "Nevada" and mean the whole thing.

*tips hat, walks back toward the mountains*
